label: H.R. 9610

latest_action.text: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 19 - 16.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 9610, the "Less Bureaucracy, Better K-12 Education Act," transfers specific elementary and secondary education functions, personnel, and funding from the Department of Education to the Department of Labor. It covers programs for disadvantaged students, migratory children, teacher training, literacy grants, charter schools, and rural education, while directing the Office of Management and Budget to ensure no net increase in federal full-time equivalent employees.

affected_groups.effect: Personnel related to elementary and secondary education functions will be transferred to the Department of Labor, and total full-time equivalent staffing levels across the impacted agencies cannot experience a net increase.
affected_groups.group: Federal Employees at the Departments of Education and Labor

affected_groups.effect: Recipients of federal K-12 formula and competitive grants, such as programs for disadvantaged students, teacher development, and rural education, will deal with the Department of Labor rather than the Department of Education for those functions.
affected_groups.group: State and Local Education Program Administrators

key_provisions: Transfers all functions and authorities of the Department of Education's Office of Elementary and Secondary Education to the Secretary of Labor.
Moves programs related to disadvantaged students, migratory children, at-risk youth, teacher development, literacy, English language acquisition, and charter schools to the Department of Labor.
Transfers all personnel, assets, liabilities, contracts, property, and unexpended appropriations associated with the moved functions to the Department of Labor.

Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to ensure that the legislation does not create a net increase in federal full-time equivalent employees and to certify compliance to congressional committees.
Ensures that existing legal documents, ongoing proceedings, pending application processes, and active lawsuits related to the transferred functions are not terminated or nullified by the transfer.
missing_information: The exact number of personnel and total dollar amounts of appropriations being transferred from the Department of Education to the Department of Labor are not specified in the text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 9610, the "Less Bureaucracy, Better K-12 Education Act," transfers specific elementary and secondary education functions, personnel, and funding from the Department of Education to the Department of Labor. It covers programs for disadvantaged students, migratory children, teacher training, literacy grants, charter schools, and rural education, while directing the Office of Management and Budget to ensure no net increase in federal full-time equivalent employees.
summary_detail.significance: This bill represents an organizational shift in federal governance by moving administrative responsibility for major elementary and secondary education programs out of the Department of Education and into the Department of Labor. The impact is primarily structural, shifting personnel, funds, and oversight authority for K-12 programs between federal agencies without altering the underlying funding levels or statutory requirements of the programs themselves.

title: Less Bureaucracy, Better K–12 Education Act
